title: A pointed smooth family of projective lines is Zariski locally trivial
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning one with a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $f:X\to S$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $\sigma:S\to X$ be a section, so $f\sigma=\mathrm{id}_S$. Suppose that for every geometric point $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ [def-weil-geometric-point] the fibre $X_{\bar s}=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is isomorphic over $\Omega$ to $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Then there is a Zariski open cover $(S_i)$ of $S$ and $S_i$-isomorphisms $X\times_SS_i\simeq\mathbf P^1_{S_i}$ that carry $\sigma|_{S_i}$ to the infinity section $[1:0]$. Each chosen pointed isomorphism remains such an isomorphism after every base change to $S_i$. No reducedness of $S$ and no residue-characteristic restriction are assumed.

source.place: Conrad, Proposition 4.2.7, proof, printed p.124, cohomology and base change applied to the inverse ideal of the section; this is the general pointed-curve input used there. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this assertion in this form.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-smooth-flat], $f$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Properness supplies quasi-compactness and separatedness, hence quasi-separatedness, so $f$ is finitely presented (the convention is locally finitely presented, quasi-compact and quasi-separated). Its geometric fibres are pure of dimension one: they are the projective lines in the hypothesis, and [lem-sc-projective-line-smooth-relative-dimension-one] identifies their relative dimension. Apply [lem-trf-geometric-pure-fibre-point-dimension] with $d=1$ to obtain $\dim_x X_{f(x)}=1$ at every $x$. Thus $f$ is smooth of relative dimension one in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Properness also supplies separatedness for the next step. If $S$ is empty the empty open cover proves the assertion; henceforth the construction is pointwise on the nonempty base.

source.place: Tag 00P4, lemma-dimension-at-a-point-preserved-field-extension, as packaged in lem-trf-geometric-pure-fibre-point-dimension; smoothness conventions from morphisms.tex.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-smooth-curve-section-cartier] to $f$ and $\sigma$. Its image $D=\sigma(S)$ is a closed effective Cartier divisor. Since $D\to S$ is the identity under $\sigma$, it is flat, so $D$ is relative effective Cartier by [def-pc-relative-effective-cartier]. Define $L=\mathcal O_X(D)=\mathcal I_D^\vee$; it is invertible by [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-invertible]. For every base change $g:T\to S$, [lem-pc-recd-pullback] applies to the flat finitely presented $f$ and this relative divisor: $D_T$ is the base-changed section and $g_X^*L\cong\mathcal O_{X_T}(D_T)$. In particular on a geometric fibre $L_{\bar s}=\mathcal O_{X_{\bar s}}(\sigma(\bar s))$. This uses relative-divisor pullback, whose base morphism is arbitrary, rather than a formula requiring $g$ flat.

source.place: Tag 067R, lemma-section-smooth-regular-immersion (relative dimension one); Tag 056Q, lemma-relative-Cartier; definition of the inverse divisor ideal in section-effective-Cartier-invertible.

proof.text: Fix a geometric fibre and an isomorphism with $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$. Its marked point is $p=[a:b]$. Choose $c,d\in\Omega$ with $ca+db=1$. The invertible coordinate change $y_0=cx_0+dx_1$, $y_1=-bx_0+ax_1$ has determinant $1$ and carries $p$ to $[1:0]$. This is a scheme isomorphism: the inverse linear substitution induces the inverse graded polynomial-ring map, and the induced degree-zero localization maps glue on the standard Proj charts. On $D_+(y_0)$ the ideal of $[1:0]$ has generator $t=y_1/y_0$, and on $D_+(y_1)$ it has generator $1$. Its dual therefore has frames $t^{-1}$ and $1$, with transition $t^{-1}=y_0/y_1$, exactly the transition of $\mathcal O(1)$ in [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Hence $L_{\bar s}\cong\mathcal O(1)$. By [lem-pc-projective-space-twist-cohomology] with $n=d=1$, its global sections have basis $y_0,y_1$, and $H^1$ is zero. The morphism of this complete linear system is an isomorphism: on its two target charts the coordinate maps are $\Omega[z]\to\Omega[t]$, $z\mapsto t$, and $\Omega[w]\to\Omega[t^{-1}]$, $w\mapsto t^{-1}$. In particular it is a closed immersion. These are explicit chart computations from the cited twist and cohomology statements, valid also in characteristic two.

source.place: Tag 01XT, lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring, specialized to n=1,d=1; standard two-chart identification of the point divisor with the degree-one twist.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-fibrewise-very-ample-evaluation] hold for $(f,L)$: $f$ is flat proper finitely presented, every geometric fibre has dimension one, and Step 3 supplies both the complete-linear-system closed immersion and $H^1=0$. It follows that $E=f_*L$ is finite locally free, its canonical base-change map $g^*E\to(f_T)_*L_T$ is invertible for every $g:T\to S$, and evaluation is a quotient $f^*E\twoheadrightarrow L$ defining a closed immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_S(E)$. The same statement identifies its base change with the complete-linear-system morphism on each geometric fibre. The rank of $E$ is two: a local free presentation of rank $r$ pulls back to $\Omega^r$, whereas base change and Step 3 identify that vector space with $\Omega^2$.

source.place: Tag 0B91, lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general, through the existing fibrewise-very-ample evaluation theorem; this implements Conrad Proposition 4.2.7, printed p.124.

proof.text: Cover $S$ by opens $U$ on which $E$ has an ordered free basis of length two. By [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], this basis identifies $\mathbf P_S(E)|_U$ with $\mathbf P^1_U$ in the quotient convention; [lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space] identifies that relative-Proj projective space with the base-change projective line of the statement. We obtain $\phi_U:X_U\to\mathbf P^1_U$. Its geometric fibres are isomorphisms by Steps 3--4. Apply [lem-sfb-universal-isomorphism-open] with $B=U$, $A=X_U$, $C=\mathbf P^1_U$, and $f=\phi_U$. The source map is flat, locally finitely presented and universally closed, by Step 1 and the restriction of properness. The target map is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], hence locally of finite type, separated and closed. The theorem gives an open $W\subseteq U$ representing the isomorphism property after every base change. Every geometric point of $U$ factors through $W$ because its fibre map is an isomorphism. Therefore $W=U$ as open subschemes; use the theorem at $\mathrm{id}_U$ to conclude that $\phi_U$ is an isomorphism, including on nilpotents.

source.place: Tag 05XD, lemma-where-isomorphism, scheme specialization; projective bundle coordinates from constructions.tex Tags 01OB and 01OE.

proof.text: It remains to adapt the frame to the section. Under the quotient classification of [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], the section $j\sigma$ corresponds to the pulled-back evaluation quotient $q:E\twoheadrightarrow M=\sigma^*L$. The module $M$ is invertible: pulling back a local rank-one frame of $L$ gives such a frame. Refine each $U$ so that $M$ has a frame $m$. If $v_0,v_1$ is the frame of $E$, write $q(v_0)=am$, $q(v_1)=bm$. Surjectivity says that at each stalk at least one of $a,b$ is a unit, so the opens where $a$ or $b$ is invertible cover $U$. Where $a$ is invertible put $e_0=a^{-1}v_0$ and $e_1=v_1-ba^{-1}v_0$. Their change-of-basis determinant is $a^{-1}$, so they form a basis, with $q(e_0)=m$ and $q(e_1)=0$. Where $b$ is invertible first interchange $v_0,v_1$ and use the same formula. The basis identification of the projective bundle then carries the section to the quotient $(1,0)$, namely $[1:0]$. Composing $j$ with these basis identifications gives the required pointed isomorphisms on the refined cover. This is a local two-by-two calculation, not an assertion that the quotient line or its kernel is globally trivial.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.7, proof, printed p.124, paragraph applying cohomology and base change to the inverse ideal of the section; details expanded here without using any SGA source.

proof.text: For a chosen pointed isomorphism $\phi_i:X\times_SS_i\to\mathbf P^1_{S_i}$ and any $h:T\to S_i$, pull back $\phi_i$ and its inverse. Their composites are the identities because the two original composites were identities. The fibre-product associativity identifies their source with $X\times_ST$; the definition [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] identifies the target with $\mathbf P^1_T$. Pulling back the equality $\phi_i\sigma_i=[1:0]$ gives the same equality for the pulled-back section. Thus every chosen isomorphism remains pointed after every base change, with no condition on reducedness, characteristic or on $T$.
